ledger.claim: The escalation the rider seeks is terminal and it is the outcome that protects the rider on this record. Under POL-NS-09 no monetary ruling issues and the disputed fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and POL-GEN-03 confirms ESCALATE always replaces the monetary ruling. The fare record as it stands shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee with payment_status 'PENDING' and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so escalation leaves the rider not carrying the contested charge while a human reviewer settles the pattern question between these two parties.

An honest concession, so that no argument is made on it: POL-NS-04 cannot carry this case. The driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 chat message at 06:52:00, twenty seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails on the chat log; and the rider's own device fixes sit 519 m from the pickup pin with a rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0 against the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so limb (c) fails affirmatively on admissible fixes. Rider-side relief therefore cannot come from POL-NS-04 and must come from escalation under POL-NS-09.

Disclosure: EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING — status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, because no traffic advisory matched this pickup road and waiting window — and its absence is itself citable. The consequence is that nothing in the record corroborates the kerbside conditions on this pickup road and the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation limb is unavailable, and any attempt to rely on limb (i) against a MISSING artifact engages POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone. The entire charge therefore rests on a single in-geofence run of 330 seconds that cleared the 300-second STANDARD minimum by only 30 seconds — one further reason this case belongs with a human reviewer rather than an automated collection.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-10T06:50:20+08:00, and the driver's own trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:50:00 — all 34 in-geofence fixes sit 24.01 m from the pin — so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are met and the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied.

The qualifying in-geofence run lasted a continuous 330 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum for this zone class — a 30-second surplus (shortfall_sec of -30.0) — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met, the dwell being measured, as the clause requires, from the first qualifying fix at 06:50:00 and not from the 06:50:20 arrival marker.

The driver terminated the trip at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — 30 seconds after the required 300-second dwell elapsed at 06:55:00 — and no boarding event is recorded, so POL-NS-01 limb (d) is met and the charge is legitimately payable by the rider.

No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the charge: POL-NS-06 only refunds where the effective dwell falls short of the minimum, and here the dwell exceeds it, so there is no shortfall to refund and the full fee stands.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival test is not engaged: at the 06:50:20 arrival marker the driver was stationary (single distinct speed of 0.0 km/h) only 24 m from the pin — inside both the arrival radius and the clause's 300 m ceiling — so the arrival marker is true and the waiting clock runs as marked.

POL-NS-04 does not apply: the rider's 06:51:40 message was answered by the driver at 06:52:00, 20 seconds later and well inside the clause's 120-second window, so limb (b) fails; and the rider's device sat 519.36 m from the pin with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0 out of 16 fixes, so limb (c) fails too.

POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance rule cannot apply: it governs only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and here the driver was inside the 50 m STANDARD radius throughout, so the arrival was at the pickup point itself and not at a wrong face of the venue.

The chat log corroborates arrival and continued coordination during the waiting window: the system's 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 06:50:21, the driver's 'At Block 612 lobby pickup' at 06:50:35 and his 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00 — the driver did everything the wait required of him.

The cancellation-fee line reconciles exactly with the fee schedule: SGD 4.00 is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the chargeable figure is sound.

Compensation is owed to the driver under POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, namely SGD 3.20, and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed_trips_30d is far below 0.08, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road or waiting window: EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 (the impairment is disclosed and the artifact carries no fact), so its absence is the only citable thing about it — the rider cannot invoke POL-NS-06(i) accumulation to manufacture a shortfall, and the driver's compliance rests on the uninterrupted 330-second hold.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case is escalated to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold. While review is pending the fee is neither collected from the rider nor refunded, and no driver compensation is paid.

WHY ESCALATE. POL-NS-09(c) is a mandatory escalation trigger and it fires. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d on EV-RPROF-09110 is 2, and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d on EV-DPROF-09110 is 2. Read together they show two or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days, and the rider's own filing describes this as 'another dispute with the same driver'. These are precisely the two fields POL-GEN-01 makes citable for this test, so nothing here rests on a context-only counter: the lifetime prior_no_show_flags field mentioned in the rider's brief is not used and carries no weight. Under POL-GEN-03 escalation is terminal and replaces any monetary outcome.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER. Whether the repeated no-show disputes between this rider and this driver (2 shown on each profile in the trailing 90 days) indicate abuse on either side or a systemic pick-up problem between these two parties, and how the held fee should be disposed of once that pattern question is settled. The reviewer receives both advocate briefs, the admissibility pre-pass report, the clauses relied on (POL-NS-01 to POL-NS-09, POL-GEN-01, POL-GEN-02, POL-GEN-03) and this reasoning.

THE DRIVER'S MERITS (made out, but the escalation is terminal). POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) all hold on admissible evidence. (a) The trip record carries the driver 'arrived' event at 06:50:20. (b) The GPS trace EV-GPS-09110 places 34 qualifying fixes at 24.01 m inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:50:00, at or before that event, so the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied. (c) The continuous in-geofence hold ran 330 seconds from 06:50:00 against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (shortfall -30.0 s, a 30-second surplus), measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival marker. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell elapsed at 06:55:00, with no boarding event recorded. POL-NS-06 gives no refund because there is no shortfall; the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the limb (i) accumulation route is unavailable and nothing may be asserted against a missing artifact. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the arrival marker the driver was stationary (single distinct speed 0.0 km/h) at 24 m, inside both the 50 m radius and the clause's 300 m ceiling, so the marker is true. POL-NS-03 cannot apply because the driver was never outside the arrival radius. The SGD 4.00 fee reconciles exactly with the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and there is no POL-NS-08(a) to (c) impairment (max GPS gap 0 s, 34 fixes across the window, 4 chat messages matching the trip record's chat_message_count of 4). Compensation under POL-NS-07 would be 80 percent of SGD 4.00, namely SGD 3.20, and the anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by 120 completed trips is far below 0.08. That compensation is withheld only because the escalation is terminal; it is not denied on the merits.

THE RIDER'S OTHER ROUTES DO NOT INDEPENDENTLY HELP. POL-NS-04 fails: the driver replied 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00, twenty seconds after the rider's 06:51:40 'Coming down now', inside the clause's 120-second window, so limb (b) fails on the chat log; and the rider's device sat 519.36 m from the pin with rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 of 16 fixes, failing limb (c) affirmatively against the 100 m STANDARD presence radius. The rider's only working route is the escalation just described.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding fact - the two-counterparty-dispute pattern - is carried by EV-RPROF-09110 and EV-DPROF-09110, two independent artifacts each at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so no separate escalation under POL-NS-09(a) is needed.

NO REFERRAL. No clause that produces a referral fires: POL-NS-05(ii) does not (qualifying in-geofence fixes exist), and POL-NS-07's packet instruction to refund the rider does not (the anti-farming check does not trip). The open question above therefore sits in this explanation, not in the referrals list.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
